case_title: Jagdish and another v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour/acquaintance; prior enmity/dispute (animosity over love letters written by the son of the second appellant to the daughter of PW-1, and earlier police cases between the parties)
weapon: Lathis, gandasi and guns (as alleged); the two appellants were armed with lathis
evidence_type: Eyewitness (solitary, PW-1); medical evidence (post-mortem injury findings); FIR; earlier police records of enmity
aggravating_circumstances: Assault by a group of 13 persons at night; eleven injuries including a bone-deep head wound and incised wounds (as alleged in the prosecution evidence)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted three accused; sentence not stated in the judgment
high_court_outcome: Acquitted one accused (Ishwar); upheld convictions of the two appellants
neutral_facts: The victim and the accused lived in the same locality and knew each other. Animosity existed because the son of one accused had written love letters to the daughter of the prosecution's eyewitness. An earlier altercation on 20 May 1995 led to police cases against both sides, and a further incident followed on 12 June 1995. On 16 June 1995, at about 9.00 p.m., the victim was returning from the eyewitness's house when the assault is said to have taken place. The prosecution alleged that thirteen persons surrounded the victim at night and attacked with lathis, gandasi and guns. The solitary eyewitness, a woman, said she was accompanied by her husband, her sister-in-law and another person, and that all of them moved away out of fear. Later, the eyewitness and her sister-in-law went to a police station about a kilometre away at about 3.00 a.m. to lodge the first information report, while the husband and the other person remained at home. The report made generalised allegations against all thirteen accused, while the eyewitness's later account attributed specific blows to each. The victim sustained eleven injuries, including a bone-deep wound to the head with damage to the brain, lacerated wounds, and a linear incised wound caused by a sharp weapon. One accused was said to have struck the victim's head with a lathi.
physical_harm: Death of the deceased; eleven injuries including a bone-deep wound to the right parieto-occipital region with damage to the brain, lacerated wounds and a linear incision from a sharp weapon
motive: alleged: animosity arising from love letters written by the son of the second appellant to the daughter of PW-1, with earlier police cases between the parties
key_evidence_accepted: Medical evidence of eleven injuries, accepted as indicating a mob assault; the Court did not accept the eyewitness account as reliable enough to sustain conviction
witness_credibility: PW-1 (sole eyewitness) severely doubted: FIR generalised, court statement more specific, delayed police visit, enmity; PW-8 wrongly treated as eyewitness by High Court, his presence disbelieved by Trial Court
bail_history: Not stated (judgment only directs that bail bonds be discharged if the accused were on bail)
trial_duration: offence: 16.06.1995; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 18.07.2008; Supreme Court: 06.08.2009
legal_representation: Appellants: S. R. Singh, Senior Advocate, with Ram Naresh Yadav and others; State: Deepak Thukral and Dr. Monika Gusain, Advocates
investigation_status: FIR lodged at about 3.00 a.m.; of 13 accused only six charge-sheeted; two tried by juvenile court; seven summoned under s.319; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Prosecution gave up two witnesses without examining them; High Court erred in treating PW-8 as an eyewitness without discussion
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted three accused. High Court: acquitted one (Ishwar), upheld the two appellants' convictions. Supreme Court: appellants acquitted, High Court order set aside
prosecution_argument: PW-1 and PW-8 were eyewitnesses; appellant no.2 gave the fatal lathi blow to the head and appellant no.1 also assaulted the deceased; street light present; PW-1's sister-relationship with the deceased does not make her evidence doubtful (Khem Karan)
defence_argument: Acquittal of co-accused bars conviction under s.149; High Court wrongly applied s.34 without charge; no common intention; PW-1 and PW-8 were not eyewitnesses; alternatively the case falls under s.304 Part II (Dalip Singh, Sakharam Nangare)
legal_principle_applied: A conviction on a solitary eyewitness is sustainable only if reliable, cogent and convincing with surrounding circumstances; such evidence requires heightened scrutiny; false implication must be considered
precedent_relied_upon: State of Rajasthan v. Bhola Singh, AIR 1994 SC 542 (relied on); Lallu Manjhi v. State of Jharkhand, (2003) 2 SCC 401 (relied on); Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1953 SC 364, Sakharam Nangare v. State of Maharashtra, (2012) 9 SCC 249, and Khem Karan v. State of U.P., (1974) 4 SCC 603 (referred to)
other_sentence_order: Appellants to be released forthwith unless required in any other case; bail bonds discharged if on bail
